did_you_know.text: Judges chapter 5 opens with a victory song by Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam, following the deliverance granted to Israel.
The song recalls the LORD’s departure from Seir and his march from the land of Edom, describing the earth trembling and the heavens pouring down rain.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath and Jael, travelers stopped using the main roads, and people had to take winding and dangerous routes instead.
The song describes a time when Israel chose other gods, while no shield or spear could be seen among them; this emphasizes the nation’s weakness before its deliverance.
Deborah calls herself to rise and sing, and Barak son of Abinoam to rise and take his captives; the song thus combines thanksgiving with a call to action.
Zebulun and Naphtali are described as tribes that risked their lives in the battle, while other tribes—including Reuben, Dan, and Asher—are mentioned for holding back or hesitating.
The kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo, but according to the song they took no silver as plunder; the battle is presented as a conflict without the usual spoils of war.
The Kishon River is described as sweeping away the enemy, while the horses and their riders are mentioned racing away in flight after the battle.
Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, receives a special blessing: the song declares her more blessed than all the women who live in tents, because of what she did to Sisera.
The song ends with a prayer for the downfall of the LORD’s enemies and compares those who love him to the sun rising in its strength. Then it states that the land had peace for forty years.
